name: Quote comparison & advice
lead: The quotes from a marketing exercise are aligned on one coverage grid, every value sourced, then checked against the needs gathered from the client. You pick the offer; the tool drafts the advice and suitability record.

project.title: Commercial package (property, business interruption, liability) marketing for Birchwood Joinery Ltd (fictional)

extracts.text: Business interruption for 12 months, including after a machinery breakdown. Machinery breakdown cover on the equipment ($410,000). Deductible: $1,000 maximum.
General liability of at least $3,000,000 per occurrence, required by the main customer's master contract. Budget: $9,500 a year at most, taxes included.
General liability $3,000,000; machinery breakdown included; business interruption 12 months; annual premium $9,400.
Standard deductible: 10% of the loss, minimum $500, maximum $3,000.
General liability $3,000,000; machinery breakdown included; business interruption 12 months; deductible $1,000; annual premium $9,100.
Business interruption following a machinery breakdown is limited to an indemnity period of 6 months.
General liability $2,000,000; machinery breakdown optional (+$650); business interruption 12 months; deductible $1,000; annual premium $8,400 without the option.
Damage to machines over 15 years old is excluded unless declared and surveyed beforehand.
Equipment: 11 machines, 2 of them over 15 years old (panel saw and jointer).

steps: Extracting cover from the 3 quotes and the policy wording
Aligning on one grid, units and deductibles normalised
Checking against the needs, contradictions flagged

contradictions.title: Northwind: the quote shows 12 months of business interruption, the wording caps it at 6 after a breakdown
contradictions.impact: The client's main need would be only half covered.
contradictions.action: Ask Northwind for a special clause, or set the offer aside.

contradictions.title: Deductibles that don't compare: percentage versus flat
contradictions.impact: On a large loss, Alder's deductible can be three times what the client asked for.
contradictions.action: Get the client's agreement and write it in the advice record.

contradictions.title: Cobalt: liability below the customer's requirement
contradictions.impact: The client could lose its main customer contract.
contradictions.action: Set the offer aside or ask for a higher limit.

contradictions.title: Cobalt: 2 machines excluded from breakdown cover
contradictions.impact: Part of the equipment would not be covered.
contradictions.action: Flag the exclusion to the client if the offer stays on the table.

contradictions.title: Chosen offer's premium within the client's budget
